exposure: Patients diagnosed with accreta preoperatively vs intraoperatively
outcome: Presence of invasive placentation on pathology report
cohort: Patients undergoing cesarean hysterectomy for suspected placenta accreta from 2000 to 2016 at Barnes-Jewish Hospital
finding: The majority of patients undergoing cesarean hysterectomy for suspected placenta accreta had the diagnosis confirmed on pathology, but intraoperative vigilance is required as the need for cesarean hysterectomy may not be anticipated preoperatively.
mod_finding: This study focuses on cesarean hysterectomy as a treatment for suspected placenta accreta and does not directly examine other modes of delivery.
